query: Fog to the Line {Professor Thorne chalks a line on the wall at shoulder height. "Water and fire together. Make fog. To the line, and not a hair over."|Fog day. Thorne's chalk line is lower than last time.|The fog line again. Thorne no longer explains; he just draws it and folds his arms.} {The windows have been shut.|Somebody's fog smells of burnt toast.|{season == "winter": The fog freezes on the windows in ferns.|The hall is warm, and the fog comes too easily.}} Balance fire and water exactly {Your fog rises, thick and white, and stops at the line as if it can read. Thorne looks at it a long time. "Hm."|Your fog fills the hall to the chalk precisely. Thorne makes a small mark in his book; you'd give a crown to know what.|You hold the balance so finely that your fog comes up the wall like a tide and stops. Thorne nods, once. From him, a standing ovation.} {Too much fire. Your fog turns to scalding steam and the front row leaves. Thorne opens a window without comment.|Too much water. A small rain falls on your desk, and only your desk, and on your hands, which are cold for an hour. Thorne writes something down.|You overshoot the line by a head and scald your wrist doing it. Thorne measures the fog with his stick, twice, in silence.} Hold the water; let a partner burn {You call the water and your partner warms it. Half the credit, half the effort, and all the mana you had.|You hold a ball of water steady for twenty minutes while your partner fusses with the flame. Your arms shake; your fog is fine.|You're the best water-holder in the class now, which Thorne calls "a respectable specialism" in a tone that isn't sure.}
